title: Preemptive lane evicter with progressive degradation and multi-region fail-safe
creator: Ava Patel
description:
Problem: During cross-region spikes and partial outage scenarios we see tail latency regressions and queue accumulation for latency-sensitive tenants. Existing token-bucket and lane-based shedding provide basic protection but lack a predictable preemptive eviction strategy that: 1) keeps SLO-bound requests flowing, 2) enables graceful fidelity degradation for long-running or batch-style requests, and 3) integrates with cross-region failover policies and circuit breakers.

Goal: Implement a preemptive lane-evicter component in the serving gateway that enforces tenant-priority bands and progressive degradation tiers. It should: (a) proactively evict or downgrade lower-priority queued requests when headroom is predicted to breach SLOs, (b) coordinate with the regional circuit-breaker to trigger controlled cross-region spillover before hard failures, and (c) expose runtime controls to allow operators to tune eviction aggressiveness per-release.

Scope: Proof-of-concept in staging followed by gradual rollout to canary fleet and regional expansion. This ticket covers design, implementation in gateway runtime, integration tests, operator playbooks, and monitoring/alerting configs. Rollout gated by canary latency metrics and synthetic traffic tests.
acceptance_criteria: A preemptive evicter running in the gateway that can be enabled via feature flag per-region and per-cluster
Eviction decisions respect tenant priority bands and configured degradation tiers (trim -> compress -> model-variant fallback)
When headroom forecast indicates >10% risk of breaching 99th-percentile latency SLO in 30s window, lower-priority queued requests are evicted/downgraded with measurable reduction in tail latency
Evicter emits structured telemetry: eviction.reason, evicted_tenant, original_route, new_route_or_fallback, predicted_risk_score
Integration with circuit-breaker: when regional circuit trips, evicter initiates soft spillover policy to remote region for P0 requests without data loss
Operator controls in Console: enable/disable, aggressiveness slider (0-100), priority band mappings, and realtime eviction rate chart
Unit and e2e tests simulate spike scenarios across two regions and validate expected behavior
Runbook updated with rollback steps and postmortem template
implementation_notes: Design: implement forecasting module using sliding-window throughput/latency metrics + lightweight AR(1) predictor to estimate headroom for next 30s
Eviction policy: deterministic ranking = tenant_priority * weight + recency_penalty + predicted_cost_score; stable ties broken by token-age to avoid starvation
Degradation ladder: 1) request trimming (truncate long prompts), 2) response compression (lower token budget), 3) fallback to quantized/model-variant, 4) evict
Circuit-breaker integration: expose gRPC hook that returns region health and suggested spillover target. Evicter consults this before promoting cross-region failover
Telemetry: add high-cardinality labels sparingly; aggregate by priority-band for dashboards; sparse sampling for full request traces
Safety: include cooldown windows per-tenant to prevent repeated evictions within 60s unless tenant continues to misbehave
Feature flags: start as experimental behind 'preemptive_evicter_v1' and 'cross_region_soft_spill' flags
Compatibility: fallback to existing token-bucket admission when feature disabled; ensure no additional p99 overhead when idle
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: false positives in eviction (evicting healthy requests) -> Mitigation: conservative default aggressiveness and holdback on canary, require two consecutive forecast windows before aggressive eviction
Risk: cross-region spill increases egress cost and data residency concerns -> Mitigation: policy whitelists for tenants allowed to spill and circuit-breaker thresholds tuned per-tenant
Risk: OOM or CPU hotspots from forecasting module -> Mitigation: implement lightweight predictor in C++ hot path and rate-limit forecasts to 1Hz per gateway instance
Risk: operator confusion -> Mitigation: Console show expected impact preview on toggle and a dry-run mode that logs decisions without enacting them
